insight.title: Why Eyeliner Was Originally Invented
insight.subtitle: An ancient Egyptian survival tool is now a staple of the modern beauty industry.

sections.text: Before it became a billion-dollar makeup staple, eyeliner was a rugged survival tool. In ancient Egypt, both men and women wore thick black kohl—not for beauty, but to survive the harsh desert sun.

The blinding glare of the Nile sun caused severe eye damage. Egyptians discovered that dark kohl around the eyes absorbed sunlight, acting exactly like the grease modern football players wear under their helmets.

Centuries later, the protective soot evolved into a symbol of status and divinity. When Western archaeologists excavated tombs in the 1920s, they brought the ancient Egyptian "smoky eye" look directly into modern fashion.
Today's hottest makeup trend started as ancient desert sunglasses.
